scope: 461 satellites of planets and Pluto, plus implemented Dimorphos and 22 selected expansion candidates; not a complete census of small-body satellites

lenses.label: Monochrome
lenses.description: Stooke’s DLR-controlled multi-mission mosaic. Source detail varies; photographed shadows and source-authored seam adjustments remain.

lenses.label: Elevation
lenses.description: Radial height above an 11.1 km reference sphere, sampled from the Ernst et al. (2023) shape model. Fixed relief lighting shows slopes; mesh spacing is about 148 m.

coreCatalog.name: Deimos
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Monochrome
lenses.description: Stooke’s Viking and MRO mosaic. Large areas have only coarse observations; source shading, seams and polar interpolation remain. The source supplies no validity mask.

lenses.label: Elevation
lenses.description: Radius above a 6.2 km reference sphere, sampled from the Ernst et al. (2023) shape model. Facets without a solved SPC albedo are conservatively withheld; the full shape includes less-constrained terrain.

coreCatalog.name: Io
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Monochrome
lenses.description: USGS Voyager/Galileo mosaic on a 1 km grid; original detail varies from about 1 to 10 km per pixel. Gray grid marks documented no-data and its resampled boundary. Photographed terrain shading remains; globe lighting is approximate.

lenses.label: Enhanced color
lenses.description: USGS enhanced-color mosaic: near-infrared, green and violet color ratios combined with observed monochrome detail. USGS corrected broad limb darkening and matched image seams. Source color detail varies from 1.3 to 21 km per pixel. Interpolated polar color is withheld; observed monochrome remains where available. Gray grid marks missing imagery. Acquisition shading, seams and changes between mission dates can remain; globe lighting is approximate.

coreCatalog.name: Europa
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Monochrome
lenses.description: USGS Voyager/Galileo mosaic. Source resolution varies from about 200 m to 20 km per pixel. Gray grid marks documented no-data and its resampled boundary. Original image shading remains; globe lighting is approximate.

lenses.label: Enhanced color
lenses.description: Galileo enhanced color: 756 nm → red, 559 nm → green, 404 nm → blue, at 1.4–1.6 km per pixel. Color covers part of the surface. A correction for each observation reduces broad photographed shading; oblique views retain observed monochrome. Overall brightness is matched to the monochrome base, preserving color ratios. Photographed shadows and seams can remain; added globe lighting is approximate. Gray grid marks gaps in both sources.

coreCatalog.name: Ganymede
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Monochrome
lenses.description: USGS Voyager/Galileo mosaic at a 1 km map grid. Original observations vary from about 400 m to 20 km per pixel. Gray grid marks documented missing imagery. Photographed terrain shading remains; added globe lighting is approximate.

lenses.label: Enhanced color
lenses.description: USGS color mosaic combines infrared, green and violet observations with sharper monochrome detail. The source is photometrically normalized and brightness matched. Monochrome remains at the poles, in missing color coverage, and across the source's 210–250° west sector whose red channel was synthesized. This is enhanced color, not natural color; source resolution and seams vary.

coreCatalog.name: Callisto
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Monochrome
lenses.description: USGS mosaic on a 1 km grid; original image resolution varies from 400 m to 60 km per pixel. USGS normalized broad illumination and matched overlapping images. Photographed relief, coarse patches and some seams remain. Gray grid marks documented no-data and its resampled boundary. Added globe lighting is approximate.

coreCatalog.name: Amalthea
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Monochrome
lenses.description: Galileo clear and green-filter images registered to the PDS Stooke shape. Bounded correction and brightness matching reduce photographed shading; raw detector brightness is not calibrated albedo. Gray grid marks unavailable or unreliable samples. Resolved detail ranges from about 2.4 to 8.3 km per source pixel.

lenses.label: Elevation
lenses.description: Radial height above an 83.5 km reference sphere from Stooke’s Voyager-derived shape model. This shows the large irregular shape, not surveyed local topography. The 5° grid includes modeled unseen terrain; the archive warns that facets and depressions may be exaggerated.

coreCatalog.name: Himalia
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Shape model
lenses.description: Approximate elongated shape using Cassini’s observed 1.25:1 outline and JPL’s size estimate. Equal short axes and the viewing orientation are assumed. The gray grid marks unmapped terrain.

coreCatalog.name: Thebe
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Monochrome
lenses.description: Galileo clear-filter observations registered to the PDS shape. Bounded illumination normalization and overlap brightness matching reduce photographed shading. This is relative image brightness, not calibrated albedo. Gray grid marks unobserved or unreliable samples; cast shadows are not reconstructed.

lenses.label: Elevation
lenses.description: Radial height above a 49.3 km reference sphere from Stooke’s Galileo-derived shape model. Shows the broad irregular shape, not local altitude above a geoid. The archived 5° grid includes modeled unseen terrain and may exaggerate depressions; it is not a high-resolution terrain survey.

coreCatalog.name: Adrastea
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Shape model
lenses.description: A triaxial ellipsoid based on the 10 × 8 × 7 km semi-axes in the IAU/WGCCRE PCK. Galileo resolved Adrastea only a few pixels across, so no craters, relief map or observed surface texture are represented. The standard gray grid marks the absence of surface imagery; shared lighting describes the model shape.

coreCatalog.name: Metis
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Monochrome
lenses.description: Galileo clear-filter images mapped onto the measured 60 × 40 × 34 km reference ellipsoid. Relative image brightness is normalized with a bounded photometric approximation. Finest sampling is about 3 km/pixel; other views are coarser. Gray grid marks unavailable or unreliable imagery. This is not a resolved terrain model or calibrated albedo.

coreCatalog.name: Mimas
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Monochrome
lenses.description: Cassini 2017 monochrome mosaic at 216 m per source pixel. Photographed shadows and variable resolution remain; Directional Shadows add approximate lighting. The surface follows a simplified version of the released 2025 shape model.

lenses.label: Enhanced color
lenses.description: Published 2014 infrared–green–ultraviolet composite, photometrically corrected by Paul Schenk. Enhanced colors exceed human vision. Source resolution varies; seams and residual photographed shading remain. The surface follows a simplified version of the released 2025 shape model.

lenses.label: Elevation
lenses.description: Color shows radial height above the PDS 198.2 km reference sphere, including Mimas’s broad oval shape. Brightness shows fixed northwest relief lighting at true height scale; Shadows adds the shared approximate directional lighting. Cassini SPC terrain model, 2025 release, about 560 m grid spacing. Gray grid marks areas outside the supplied raster; no terrain is invented. The surface follows a simplified version of the released 2025 shape model.

coreCatalog.name: Enceladus
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Monochrome
lenses.description: Schenk and McKinnon (2024) controlled mosaic. Original 100 m grid delivered at about 197 m per equatorial texel. Source resolution and photographed shadows vary; globe Shadows add approximate lighting. Gray grid marks source no-data.

lenses.label: Elevation
lenses.description: Color shows height above the 256.2 × 251.4 × 248.6 km reference ellipsoid. Colors saturate below −1 and above +1 km. Brightness shows relief under fixed northwest light, without height exaggeration. Gray grid marks missing model values. The 200 m grid contains stereogrammetric and photogrammetric terrain estimates; effective detail varies.

lenses.label: Enhanced color

lenses.label: Elevation

coreCatalog.name: Titan
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Near-infrared
lenses.description: USGS 2026 controlled mosaic. Infrared reveals surface features through the haze. Image brightness is display-stretched; source haze, clouds, variable resolution and seams remain. Gray grid marks missing observations. Added globe lighting is approximate.

lenses.label: Radar
lenses.description: Cassini RADAR Team mosaic through T126. Brightness shows radar backscatter, not visible color or elevation. Gray grid marks missing measurements. The 1.4 km archive grid is prepared at 1.98 km per equatorial texel; native observation resolution varies. Shared globe Shadows remain an approximate visualization.

coreCatalog.name: Hyperion
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Monochrome
lenses.description: Cassini clear-filter imagery projected onto the measured irregular shape. Bounded correction reduces photographed shading; fine crater shadows remain. Coverage and resolution vary, and unavailable regions are marked.

lenses.label: Elevation
lenses.description: Radius above a 135 km reference sphere from the Cassini stereo and limb shape model. This shows global relief and elongation, not a finely resolved terrain DEM; shape uncertainty reaches 6 km on the less-observed side.

coreCatalog.name: Iapetus
coreCatalog.nextAction: Maintain; qualification not reassessed in this inventory

lenses.label: Monochrome
lenses.description: USGS May 2008 Cassini/Voyager mosaic at 803 m per source pixel (5760 × 2880), resampled into the shared texture layout. No additional detail is created. Coarse polar coverage, source seams and photographed shading remain; gray grid marks explicit no-data. Shared Shadows adds approximate globe lighting. Mean-radius sphere: the real equatorial ridge does not change the silhouette.

lenses.label: Enhanced color
lenses.description: Published 2014 enhanced-color Cassini composite, photometrically corrected by Paul Schenk, with nominal 400 m source pixels. Colors extend into ultraviolet and infrared. The dark leading hemisphere is real surface albedo, not a shadow or missing imagery. All supplied pixels are preserved; coarse patches and residual photographed shading remain. Shared Shadows and globe lighting remain active; shape is approximated by a sphere.

lenses.description: A flattened ellipsoid using the 54×50×26 km semi-axes measured by Karkoschka (2003) from Voyager 2 observations. Thalassa is only a few pixels across in the available images, often with motion trails, so those pixels cannot supply a registered terrain map. The standard gray grid marks unavailable surface imagery. Shared lighting describes the model shape; no craters or photographic detail are invented.

lenses.label: Shape model
lenses.description: A triaxial ellipsoid fitted to Voyager images by Karkoschka (2003), with semi-axes of 90 × 74 × 64 km. The 74 km radius sets the scene scale and is not a replacement for the three measured axes.

lenses.description: An approximate ellipsoid based on the 10.6 × 6.0 × 5.3 km dimensions presented by Porter and colleagues in 2025. lenses.label: Shape
lenses.description: The shared grid marks unavailable surface imagery over the released DART v004 global shape. DRACO and LICIACube observations constrain different regions; the closed mesh also contains modeled terrain. It represents the encounter-era body, not a measured post-impact surface. Lighting uses an arbitrary display phase about the observed pole; no photographic texture or albedo is shown.

lenses.label: Elevation
lenses.description: Color shows source-mesh radius minus a 75 m reference sphere, including the overall flattened shape. It is not height above an equipotential or a map of impact-induced change. Terrain coverage and precision follow the published encounter model. Cartographic relief and optional Sun lighting are display treatments.

limits: Counts establish registered standalone packages, not current release readiness or deployment.
Imagery lens does not imply complete coverage, true color, measured terrain or a successful new browser audit.
Absent implementation does not establish absent scientific data.
Snapshot JSON is historical evidence; the Markdown document is the editable tracker.
